name: Queen's Gambit Declined
tagline: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6: a classical, rock-solid answer to 1.d4.
description: A complete Black repertoire against 1.d4 built on the Queen's Gambit Declined. You hold the centre with ...d5 and ...e6, develop with ...Nf6, ...Be7 and ...O-O, and free your game with the Lasker idea ...h6 and ...Ne4 or the breaks ...c5, ...dxc4 and ...e5. Against the London, Colle, Jobava and other systems without c4 you use the same ...e6 and ...c5 set-up, so the plans carry over. It suits players who like sound positions and clear plans over long forced lines.

chapters.name: Orthodox: 4.Bg5
chapters.intro: The classical main line. White pins the f6 knight and builds a solid centre. We break the pin with ...Be7, castle, and ask the bishop with ...h6. If it retreats to h4, the Lasker idea ...Ne4 trades two pairs of minor pieces and frees our position. If White takes on f6 instead, we get the bishop pair and free ourselves with ...c6, ...Nd7, ...dxc4 and ...e5 or ...c5. Our problem piece is the c8 bishop: every plan aims to give it a diagonal, either with ...b6 and ...Bb7 or after ...e5.

lines.name: Lasker: 9.cxd5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. c4 { The Queen's Gambit. White offers the c-pawn to pull our d-pawn away from the centre. } 2... e6 { The Queen's Gambit Declined. d5 is backed up by a pawn and the f8 bishop can develop. The price is that the c8 bishop is shut in for now. } 3. Nc3 { Adds a second attacker to d5. } 3... Nf6 { Develop and guard d5 again. } 4. Bg5 { Pins the knight that defends d5. } 4... Be7 { Breaks the pin. If White takes on f6, the bishop recaptures and our pawns stay intact. } 5. e3 O-O { Castle first: the king is safe and the f8 rook can come to the centre later. } 6. Nf3 h6 { Ask the bishop. If it retreats to h4, the Lasker idea ...Ne4 comes; if it takes on f6, we get the bishop pair. } 7. Bh4 Ne4 { The Lasker Defence. The knight offers trades, and every trade gives our cramped pieces more room. } 8. Bxe7 Qxe7 { Recapture with the queen. Next ...Nxc3, then ...c6 or ...dxc4 to free the position. } 9. cxd5 Nxc3 { Trade first, so White has to recapture with the b-pawn. } 10. bxc3 exd5 { Recapture with the e-pawn: the c8 bishop's diagonal is open at last. } 11. Qb3 { Hits b7 and d5. } 11... Rd8 { Protects d5. The b7 pawn is covered by the c8 bishop. } 12. c4 dxc4 13. Bxc4 Nc6 { Develop with pressure on d4. Next ...Bg4 or ...Be6, and the c8 bishop is free. }

quiz.question: What is the main drawback of 2...e6?
options: The c8 bishop is shut in behind the e6 pawn
Black can no longer castle short
The f8 bishop has no squares
quiz.explanation: The e6 pawn blocks the c8 bishop. Most QGD plans, ...b6 and ...Bb7 or ...dxc4 and ...e5, are about giving that bishop a job.

quiz.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bh4 Ne4
quiz.question: What is the idea of 7...Ne4?
options: To trade minor pieces and free Black's cramped position
To prepare ...f5 and a kingside attack
quiz.explanation: After Bxe7 Qxe7 and ...Nxc3, two pairs of minor pieces are gone. With fewer pieces, Black's lack of space matters much less.

quiz.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bxf6 Bxf6 8. Rc1 c6 9. Bd3 Nd7 10. O-O dxc4 11. Bxc4
quiz.question: What is Black's freeing move?
quiz.explanation: ...e5 hits d4, opens the diagonal for the c8 bishop and wakes up the f6 bishop. Black has no problems after it.

chapters.name: Exchange Variation
chapters.intro: After cxd5 exd5 the pawns are locked in the Carlsbad structure. Our d5 pawn is solid and the c8 bishop is free at last. White's typical plan is the minority attack with b4-b5 to give us a weak c-pawn; ours is to develop with ...Be7, ...O-O, ...Nbd7, ...Re8, ...c6 and ...Nf8, then bring the knight to g6 or e6 and use the e-file. Against an early Bf4 we play ...c6 and ...Bf5 to trade White's good light-squared bishop.

quiz.question: Where is Black's d7 knight heading?
quiz.explanation: With the rook on e8, the knight can go to f8, where it defends h7, and then to g6 or e6 where it is active.

quiz.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Bf4
quiz.question: What is Black's simplest plan against 5.Bf4?
quiz.explanation: Without a white bishop on g5 there is nothing to fear on f6, so the c8 bishop comes straight out to f5, supported by ...c6.

chapters.name: Bf4, e3 and the Catalan
chapters.intro: With Nf3 White keeps many options. Against Bf4 instead of Bg5 we castle and strike with ...c5: after dxc5 Bxc5 our bishop is active and ...Nc6 and ...Qa5 follow. Against a quiet e3 we take on c4 once White's bishop has moved, then play ...c5 and ...a6 for an easy, active game. Against the Catalan with g3 and Bg2 we take on c4 and hold the pawn with ...a6 and ...b5 while it is safe, then put our bishop on b7 to fight White's g2 bishop. Many move orders, such as 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Bg5, lead back to the Orthodox chapter.

White's bishop goes to g2 to aim at our queenside. } 4... Be7 5. Bg2 O-O 6. O-O dxc4 { Take the pawn: White has to spend time winning it back, and we use that time to develop. } 7. Ne5 Nc6 { Develop and challenge the e5 knight. } 8. Bxc6 bxc6 9. Nxc6 Qe8 { The queen attacks the c6 knight. } 10. Nxe7+ Qxe7 { Material is level, White has given up the g2 bishop, and our c8 bishop is free to go to a6 or b7. }

lines.name: Catalan: 7.Qa4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. c4 { The Queen's Gambit. White offers the c-pawn to pull our d-pawn away from the centre. } 2... e6 { The Queen's Gambit Declined. d5 is backed up by a pawn and the f8 bishop can develop. The price is that the c8 bishop is shut in for now. } 3. Nf3 { Flexible: White keeps both Nc3 and g3 in reserve. } 3... Nf6 4. g3 { The Catalan. White's bishop goes to g2 to aim at our queenside. } 4... Be7 5. Bg2 O-O 6. O-O dxc4 { Take the pawn: White has to spend time winning it back, and we use that time to develop. } 7. Qa4 a6 { If White takes on c4, ...b5 gains time on the queen. } 8. Qxc4 b5 { Gain time on the queen and prepare ...Bb7. } 9. Qc2 Bb7 { The bishop fights White's g2 bishop on the long diagonal. }

lines.name: Catalan: 7.Nc3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. c4 { The Queen's Gambit. White offers the c-pawn to pull our d-pawn away from the centre. } 2... e6 { The Queen's Gambit Declined. d5 is backed up by a pawn and the f8 bishop can develop. The price is that the c8 bishop is shut in for now. } 3. Nf3 { Flexible: White keeps both Nc3 and g3 in reserve. } 3... Nf6 4. g3 { The Catalan. White's bishop goes to g2 to aim at our queenside. } 4... Be7 5. Bg2 O-O 6. O-O dxc4 { Take the pawn: White has to spend time winning it back, and we use that time to develop. } 7. Nc3 Nc6 { Develop and hit d4. } 8. e4 Rb8 { Moves the rook off the long diagonal and prepares ...b5 to hold the c4 pawn. }

lines.name: 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Bf4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. c4 { The Queen's Gambit. White offers the c-pawn to pull our d-pawn away from the centre. } 2... e6 { The Queen's Gambit Declined. d5 is backed up by a pawn and the f8 bishop can develop. The price is that the c8 bishop is shut in for now. } 3. Nf3 { Flexible: White keeps both Nc3 and g3 in reserve. } 3... Nf6 4. Bf4 Be7 { The same calm development as against Bg5. } 5. e3 O-O 6. Nc3 c5 { Strike at the centre at once. ...Nc6 and ...Qa5 follow. }

lines.name: 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.e3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. c4 { The Queen's Gambit. White offers the c-pawn to pull our d-pawn away from the centre. } 2... e6 { The Queen's Gambit Declined. d5 is backed up by a pawn and the f8 bishop can develop. The price is that the c8 bishop is shut in for now. } 3. Nf3 { Flexible: White keeps both Nc3 and g3 in reserve. } 3... Nf6 4. e3 Be7 5. Nc3 O-O 6. Bd3 dxc4 { Take now that White's bishop has moved: it has to spend another move to recapture. } 7. Bxc4 c5 { Hit d4. } 8. O-O a6 { Prepares ...b5 with tempo on the bishop, then ...Bb7. }

lines.name: 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Bg5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. c4 { The Queen's Gambit. White offers the c-pawn to pull our d-pawn away from the centre. } 2... e6 { The Queen's Gambit Declined. d5 is backed up by a pawn and the f8 bishop can develop. The price is that the c8 bishop is shut in for now. } 3. Nf3 { Flexible: White keeps both Nc3 and g3 in reserve. } 3... Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O { Castle. After Nc3 and ...h6 we are back in the Orthodox main line. } 6. Nc3 h6 { Ask the bishop. If it retreats to h4, the Lasker idea ...Ne4 comes; if it takes on f6, we get the bishop pair. }

quiz.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Be7 5. Bf4 O-O 6. e3
quiz.question: What is Black's thematic move here?
quiz.explanation: With the bishop on f4 instead of g5, ...c5 hits d4 at once. After dxc5 Bxc5 Black's pieces are active.

quiz.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. e3 Be7 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Bd3
quiz.question: Why does Black take on c4 now?
options: White's bishop has already moved, so recapturing costs White another move
To win a pawn for good
quiz.explanation: Bd3 followed by Bxc4 means the bishop moved twice. Black uses the time for ...c5 and ...a6.

quiz.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. g3 Be7 5. Bg2 O-O 6. O-O dxc4 7. Qc2
quiz.question: How does Black keep the c4 pawn for now?
quiz.explanation: After ...a6, Qxc4 runs into ...b5 with tempo, and the bishop comes to b7 to fight the g2 bishop.

chapters.name: London, Jobava and Veresov
chapters.intro: Against the London we set up with ...Nf6, ...e6, ...c5 and ...Nc6, then ...Bd6 to challenge White's best bishop. If White keeps it with Bg3, we castle and play ...b6 and ...Bb7. If White trades on d6, our queen recaptures and ...e5 frees the game. Against the Jobava with Nc3 and Bf4 we play ...a6 first, so the knight can never jump to b5, then ...e6, ...c5 and queenside space with ...c4 and ...b5. Against the Veresov with Nc3 and Bg5 we develop with ...Nbd7 and ...h6, and meet f3 and e4 with ...c6 and ...e5.

lines.name: London: 7.Bg3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nf3 Nf6 { Develop and control e4. } 3. Bf4 { The London System. } 3... e6 { The same solid pawn on e6 as in the main lines. Next ...c5 and ...Nc6. } 4. e3 c5 { Hit d4, the base of White's pawn chain. } 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Bd6 { Offer to trade White's best minor piece, the f4 bishop. } 7. Bg3 O-O 8. Bd3 b6 { Prepare ...Bb7: our light-squared bishop gets a good diagonal. ...Qe7 and ...e5 are also ideas. }

lines.name: London: 7.Bxd6
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nf3 Nf6 { Develop and control e4. } 3. Bf4 { The London System. } 3... e6 { The same solid pawn on e6 as in the main lines. Next ...c5 and ...Nc6. } 4. e3 c5 { Hit d4, the base of White's pawn chain. } 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Bd6 { Offer to trade White's best minor piece, the f4 bishop. } 7. Bxd6 Qxd6 8. Bd3 e5 { The freeing break: with the f4 bishop gone, nothing stops ...e5. }

lines.name: London: 2.Bf4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Bf4 Nf6 3. e3 e6 4. Nf3 c5 { Hit d4, the base of White's pawn chain. } 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Bd6 { Offer to trade White's best minor piece, the f4 bishop. } 7. Bg3 O-O

lines.name: London: 5.Bb5+
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nf3 Nf6 { Develop and control e4. } 3. Bf4 { The London System. } 3... e6 { The same solid pawn on e6 as in the main lines. Next ...c5 and ...Nc6. } 4. e3 c5 { Hit d4, the base of White's pawn chain. } 5. Bb5+ Bd7 { Block and offer to trade our worst piece, the c8 bishop. } 6. Bxd7+ Nbxd7 { Recapture with the knight. ...Bd6 and castling are next, and our bad bishop is gone. }

lines.name: Jobava: 3...a6
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nc3 { White blocks the c-pawn and prepares Bf4 or Bg5. } 2... Nf6 3. Bf4 { The Jobava London: with Nc3 and Bf4, White wants Nb5 against c7. } 3... a6 { Takes b5 away from the knight, so Nb5 never comes. } 4. e3 e6 5. Nf3 c5 { Strike at d4, with ...Nc6 next. } 6. Bd3 Nc6 7. O-O c4 { Gain space with tempo on the bishop. The queenside pawns roll on with ...b5, already supported by ...a6. } 8. Be2 b5 { Next ...Bb7 and ...Be7. Our queenside space makes up for the open e5 square. }

lines.name: Jobava: 4.e4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Bf4 Nf6 3. Nc3 a6 { Takes b5 away from the knight, so Nb5 never comes. } 4. e4 dxe4 { Accept: White gives a pawn for activity. } 5. f3 exf3 6. Nxf3 e6 { Solid: we keep the extra pawn and develop with ...Be7 and ...O-O. }

lines.name: Veresov: 4.Nf3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nc3 { White blocks the c-pawn and prepares Bf4 or Bg5. } 2... Nf6 3. Bg5 { The Veresov. White plans f3 and e4. } 3... Nbd7 { Covers f6, so Bxf6 can be met by ...Nxf6, and prepares ...e5 if White plays e4. } 4. Nf3 h6 { Ask the bishop. } 5. Bh4 e6 6. e3 Be7 { Solid development: castle next, then ...c5. }

lines.name: Veresov: 4.f3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nc3 { White blocks the c-pawn and prepares Bf4 or Bg5. } 2... Nf6 3. Bg5 { The Veresov. White plans f3 and e4. } 3... Nbd7 { Covers f6, so Bxf6 can be met by ...Nxf6, and prepares ...e5 if White plays e4. } 4. f3 c6 { Supports d5 and gives the queen b6 against b2. } 5. e4 dxe4 6. fxe4 e5 { The key break: hit d4 while White's king is still in the centre. }

quiz.question: Black plays 3...a6. What does it prevent?
quiz.explanation: In the Jobava London the c3 knight jumps to b5 and, with the f4 bishop, attacks c7. ...a6 takes that square away for good.

quiz.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bf4 e6 4. e3 c5 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Bd6 7. Bxd6 Qxd6 8. Bd3
quiz.question: What is Black's freeing break?
quiz.explanation: The f4 bishop used to control e5. Once it is traded, ...e5 frees Black's game and opens the c8 bishop.

quiz.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. Bg5 Nbd7 4. f3 c6 5. e4 dxe4 6. fxe4
quiz.question: What is Black's best move?
quiz.explanation: White's centre looks big, but ...e5 attacks d4 at once while White's king is still in the middle.

chapters.name: Colle, Torre and Other Systems
chapters.intro: The Colle and Zukertort set up e3, Bd3 and Nbd2, aiming for e4 or a knight on e5. We use the same plan as against the London: ...e6, ...c5, ...Nc6, ...Bd6 and castle. When White pushes e4, release the tension in the centre and use our active pieces. Against the Torre with Bg5 we develop with ...Be7 and castle. Against the Blackmar-Diemer Gambit, 2.e4, we take the pawn and develop with ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...Be7.

lines.name: Colle: 8.dxc5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nf3 Nf6 { Develop and control e4. } 3. e3 { The Colle or Zukertort set-up: Bd3, castling and an e4 or Ne5 plan. } 3... e6 4. Bd3 c5 { Hit d4 before White's set-up is complete. } 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Bd6 { The bishop controls e5 and aims at White's king. } 7. O-O O-O 8. dxc5 Bxc5 9. e4 Qc7 { Controls e5 and lines up on the c7-h2 diagonal. Next ...dxe4 or ...Ng4, and ...Rd8. }

lines.name: Colle: 8.e4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nf3 Nf6 { Develop and control e4. } 3. e3 { The Colle or Zukertort set-up: Bd3, castling and an e4 or Ne5 plan. } 3... e6 4. Bd3 c5 { Hit d4 before White's set-up is complete. } 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Bd6 { The bishop controls e5 and aims at White's king. } 7. O-O O-O 8. e4 cxd4 { Release the tension first. } 9. cxd4 dxe4 10. Nxe4 Nxe4 11. Bxe4 h6 { Keep White's bishop off g5. White is left with an isolated pawn on d4; our plan is ...Bd7, ...Rc8 and trading pieces. }

lines.name: Zukertort: 5.b3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nf3 Nf6 { Develop and control e4. } 3. e3 { The Colle or Zukertort set-up: Bd3, castling and an e4 or Ne5 plan. } 3... e6 4. Bd3 c5 { Hit d4 before White's set-up is complete. } 5. b3 { The Zukertort: the bishop goes to b2 to aim at our king. } 5... Nc6 6. O-O Bd6 7. Bb2 O-O { Same set-up. Next ...b6 and ...Bb7, or ...Qe7 and ...e5. }

lines.name: 2.e3 Nf6 3.Bd3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. e3 Nf6 3. Bd3 c5 { Hit d4 before White gets c3 and f4 in. } 4. c3 Nc6 5. f4 Bg4 { The Stonewall. Our bishop gets out with tempo on the queen, before ...e6 shuts it in. }

lines.name: Torre: 3.Bg5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nf3 Nf6 { Develop and control e4. } 3. Bg5 { The Torre: the bishop pins the knight. } 3... e6 4. e3 c5 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Be7 { Unpin; if White takes on f6 we recapture with the bishop. } 7. Bd3 O-O { Castled. ...b6 and ...Bb7, or ...h6, come next. }

lines.name: 3.g3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. Nf3 Nf6 { Develop and control e4. } 3. g3 e6 4. Bg2 Be7 5. O-O O-O 6. c4 dxc4 { Take the pawn: White has to spend time winning it back, and we use that time to develop. }

lines.name: Blackmar-Diemer: 4.f3 exf3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. e4 { The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit. White gives a pawn for quick development and open lines. } 2... dxe4 { Take it. With careful development we keep the extra pawn or return it at a good moment. } 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 e6 { Solid: our pieces come out fast and we keep the extra pawn. } 6. Bg5 Be7 7. Bd3 Nc6 { Develop with pressure on d4. }

lines.name: Blackmar-Diemer: 3.f3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. e4 { The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit. White gives a pawn for quick development and open lines. } 2... dxe4 { Take it. With careful development we keep the extra pawn or return it at a good moment. } 3. f3 e5 { Hit back in the centre. After dxe5 Qxd1+ White cannot castle. } 4. dxe5 Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1 Nc6 { Attack e5. White's king is stuck in the centre. }

lines.name: Blackmar-Diemer: 4.Bg5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 { Black claims the centre at once, mirroring White. } 2. e4 { The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit. White gives a pawn for quick development and open lines. } 2... dxe4 { Take it. With careful development we keep the extra pawn or return it at a good moment. } 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Bf5 { Develop and keep the extra pawn on e4. }

quiz.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. e3 e6 4. Bd3
quiz.question: What is Black's main pawn break against the Colle?
quiz.explanation: ...c5 hits d4 at once. With ...Nc6 and ...Bd6 next, Black is ready to meet White's e4 plan.
